name: Drop Serve
summary: The drop serve lets you drop the ball, let it bounce, and hit the serve off the bounce. Because the ball has bounced, none of the volley serve restrictions apply — no below-the-waist contact, no upward swing, no paddle-below-wrist. That freedom is why it is worth knowing even if you serve well already.
whenToUse: You want topspin on the serve, which the volley serve motion makes awkward.
The below-the-waist rule keeps costing you faults, or you are worried it will.
You are returning from an injury and a normal service motion hurts.
You want a second serve shape to show, so the returner cannot settle.
howTo: Hold the ball out and let it fall from its natural height — you may not toss it up or throw it down.
Let it bounce anywhere behind the baseline, as high or low as it lands.
Step in and hit it like a groundstroke, with any swing you like.
Brush up the back of the ball if you want topspin, which makes it dip and kick.
Aim deep, toward the returner's backhand, as with any serve.
Recover behind the baseline and split-step as they return.
commonMistakes: Tossing the ball up or bouncing it down, both of which make the serve a fault.
Letting it bounce so low that the contact point is uncomfortable — release from higher.
Assuming the below-the-waist rule still applies and hitting a cramped serve anyway.
Trying so much topspin that the serve lands halfway up the service box.
Using it as a novelty rather than picking one serve and getting good at it.

drills.name: Drop, bounce, deep
drills.description: Twenty serves from the drop, all aimed at the deep third of the service box. Have somebody watch the release and call any toss or throw-down, because it is hard to feel.

drills.name: Same target, two serves
drills.description: Alternate a volley serve and a drop serve at the same target. If the drop serve is consistently shorter, you are lifting rather than driving through it.

rows.label: How the ball starts
rows.self: Dropped from your hand and allowed to bounce.
rows.other: Struck out of the air before it bounces.

rows.label: Restrictions
rows.self: None on the swing — the bounce removes them.
rows.other: Below the waist, paddle below the wrist, upward swing.

rows.label: Spin
rows.other: Hard to generate much of anything.

rows.label: Fault risk
rows.self: Only in the release: no toss, no throw-down.
rows.other: Contact height and paddle angle, judged live.

rows.label: Worth it when
rows.self: You want spin or the height rule keeps catching you.
rows.other: You already have a repeatable deep serve.
